title: Crossplane concurrency-safe hotpatch sequencing and customer communication
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Why: Recent incidents exposed a race between concurrent, partially-overlapping model rollouts and emergency hotpatches that caused tenant-visible regressions (inconsistent KV cache holders + split traffic). This ticket defines a concurrency-safe sequencing mechanism (crossplane lock + staged hotpatch pipeline), an operational runbook, and tenant-facing communication templates to reduce blast radius across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Scope: orchestration primitives (global roll-control lock, per-plane fencing), console affordances for staging/locking, API guardrails for hotpatch sequencing, synthetic rehydration jobs, and pre-approved customer comm templates. Out of scope: downstream per-model architecture changes beyond kernel selection logic.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled hotpatch sequence can be initiated via Console and API with handshake/lock acquisition across Hosted/Dedicated/Private planes
Automated dry-run mode validates kvcache reconciliation steps without impacting live traffic
Synthetic rehydration restores per-tenant KV prefixes within SLO window in at most two rollback attempts
Console shows lock owner, pending patches, and expected timeline; UI prevents concurrent conflicting patches
Runbook validated in a 1-hour tabletop with SRE, Platform, Support, and 2 customer success reps
Telemetry and alerts added: crossplane-lock-failures, stale-kvcache-detection, and staged-patch-progress metrics
runbook_steps: 1) Preflight: run 'patch-check' dry-run which simulates model variant swap and computes expected KV invalidations
2) Acquire crossplane roll lock: API call to /orchestrator/acquire?owner=<run-id> with 30s retry/backoff
3) Stage artifacts to 'staging' bucket and record metadata (model hash, quantization profile, compatible kernel set)
4) Freeze routing slices for impacted tenants (console 'slice-fence' action) and enable prefix-preserve mode where possible
5) Apply hotpatch to non-production plane imaging lanes, run smoke-kv-rehydrate with synthetic traces
6) Promote to canary slice (1-5% traffic) and monitor synthetic + customer metrics for 10 minutes
7) If anomalies, execute fast-fallback: unpin new variant and rehydrate KV from snapshot; if transient, pursue targeted rehydration flow
8) Release lock and publish timeline/status to affected tenant channels via pre-approved templates
rollback_strategy: Immediate rollback: unpin variant and route traffic to last-known-good model within the crossplane lock
Staged rollback: evacuate tenants from newly-affected hosts to warm standby pools, reduce concurrency and rehydrate KV prefixes
Fallback variant path: automatically route to quantized-compatible variant in cheaper tier when primary fails
Post-rollback reconciliation: run kvcache-audit to detect missed mutations and schedule replays to ensure determinism
communications_templates: Initial customer notice (short): We're investigating an elevated error rate for model generation; we've initiated a controlled rollback for affected customers and will provide updates every 15 minutes.
Post-mitigation notice: We completed a rollback and validated restored behavior. Root cause analysis will follow with action items and ETA for fixes.

Dedicated/Private customer specific: We require a maintenance window to apply a safe hotpatch; please confirm availability for a 15-minute window. Sensitive data handling: we will not export tenant data.
